title: Project Osmos feasibility and safe routing boundary
summary: Project Osmos is a Fabric-hosted autonomous data-engineering agent with a documented upstream task interface and specialized MWC authentication. Read-only discovery was verified live; built-in Fabio task mutations remain deferred pending a dedicated supported transport, state/recovery and safety contract. Do not invent fabio osmos commands or install/run upstream tools automatically.

decision.reason: A working upstream task interface is not yet a complete versioned Fabio integration contract. Keep deterministic Fabio artifact/data operations separate from remotely autonomous tasks until lifecycle, authentication, recovery and safety are implemented and tested explicitly.

validation.scope: Owned disposable workspace/lakehouse only. Workspace/lakehouse GET, Power BI authentication and MWC exchange, then one workload task collection GET succeeded. The exchange used the documented narrow cluster-authorization fallback to a trusted observed home cluster. No redirects followed or tokens/routes/task contents published; no task created, messaged, run, cancelled or deleted.
validation.limitation: This one-off feasibility probe is not a shipped Fabio client, execution-capacity approval, regional/cloud coverage guarantee or autonomous-task lifecycle acceptance.

interface: The current upstream skill documents PUT task creation/update, GET status/list/messages, POST messages/run/cancel and DELETE permanent task removal. /tasks is the current collection; legacy /aichat can address the same tasks without migration. This is a real interface, not evidence that no API exists.

Authentication differs from generic Fabric REST: obtain a Power BI audience bearer, read selected workspace/lakehouse/capacity context, exchange for an MWC token, and use Authorization: mwctoken with the returned TargetUriHost. Never send a generic Fabric bearer directly to a guessed workload URL.

The upstream auth reference calls the public MWC exchange example an implementation example, not a complete versioned REST contract. Retain the selected tenant/environment and validate trusted HTTPS workload origins before forwarding credentials. Do not construct workload hosts from capacity names/IDs or follow redirects. Only the narrow documented cluster-authorization condition permits a trusted observed home-cluster exchange retry.

Remote tasks can continue after the local client disconnects and can modify multiple authorized resources; the default Spark lakehouse is not the whole access boundary. Cancellation does not undo prior writes. Preserve task/message/dedup IDs, routing and recovery state; never recreate a task merely because a submission timed out.
routing: Use the upstream project-osmos skill from Microsoft Skills for Fabric when the user explicitly chooses an autonomous end-to-end lakehouse/Spark/notebook outcome. Ask permission before installing/updating/enabling a plugin, using an existing verified installation where available; do not download or execute returned instructions automatically.

Keep deterministic Fabio notebook/Spark/lakehouse/pipeline commands for explicitly scoped operations. Fabric data-agent is a data Q&A item, not the Project Osmos task service. Power BI/semantic models, warehouse T-SQL and KQL/Eventstream tasks remain with their corresponding Fabio workloads.

Before an authorized upstream execution, review the complete outcome, resources, write/overwrite/schema-evolution policy, artifact expectations and capacity consumption. Missing or unknown eligibility is not approval; do not reassign workspaces, buy capacity or weaken policy to manufacture support. No interactive prompt or guessed force/consent flag is added to Fabio.
integration_gates: Confirm a maintainer-supported versioned auth/routing/response contract and cloud/region/identity coverage; MWC credentials must stay out of argv, stdout, logs and persisted recovery files.
Implement a dedicated trusted HTTPS/no-redirect transport, bounded status/message reads and explicit execution-capacity checks, separate from inspection authentication.

Design durable task/message identities, partial create-message-run reconciliation and same-task resume/cancel/delete semantics. No automatic replay, task recreation, route migration or identity switching on uncertainty.

Ship canonical non-interactive dry-run/readonly/destructive metadata/agent-notice guards and exact task scope/identity guards. Review irreversible delete, in-flight cancel and autonomous writes separately; cancellation is not rollback.

Add hermetic unit/CLI e2e coverage and an explicitly approved disposable live create/message/run/status/cancel/delete pilot with verified cleanup and bounded cost before publishing lifecycle commands. Read-only listing alone does not satisfy this gate.
